use_when: Use it for one status that sits outside a field, such as a failed sign-in or a booking hold.
Use Warning when the person can continue and should pay attention.
Use Error when something failed and they have to act. Use Info for neutral information.

dont_use_when.when: Do not use it as the helper under a field. A field error stays on the input.
Do not put two statuses in one banner.
Do not detach the instance to recolor the fill, border, or icon.
Do not fix the height. A longer message has to grow the banner.
Do not swap in a decorative icon. The mark should name the status.

variant_intent.State=Warning: Use Warning when the person can continue and should pay attention.
variant_intent.State=Error: Use Error when something failed and they have to act. Use Info for neutral information.
variant_intent.State=Info: Use Error when something failed and they have to act. Use Info for neutral information.
variant_intent.Show icon: Leave Show icon on unless the message already names the status.

placement: Under the heading and explanation it reports on, above the actions: in the Figma 'Component Appearance' example the Error banner sits above the buttons 'Try Google again', 'Continue with Apple' and 'Use email and password'.
Width follows its container: let the banner fill the width of its container (Figma Best Practice).

a11y.fact: role="alert" for Error and role="status" for Warning and Info; role can be set to none to opt out.
The icon area is decorative (aria-hidden); the message carries the meaning.
Do not rely on color alone. The message has to say what happened.
